name: ocean-surface
title: Ocean Surface
blurb: Open-sea tile driven by four Gerstner swells whose phase is computed in world space, so tiles placed edge-to-edge join seamlessly. Sea state 0–9 (Beaufort) scales height, steepness, wind streaks and whitecaps; rain prints rings on the surface; optional seabed, water-column cut-away and bioluminescent crests at night.

name: beach-shore
title: Beach & Surf
blurb: Sandy beach profile from an offshore bar to the dunes. Shoaling Gerstner waves steepen over the bar, roll in as foam lines and run up the slope as swash before draining back — the waterline moves because the animated sea genuinely intersects the sand. Wet-sand band, wrack line, driftwood, shells, rocks, swaying dune grass and palms.

name: sea-cliff-arch
title: Sea Cliff & Arch
blurb: Eroding headland with a wave-cut platform, a natural sea arch and a detached sea stack. Swell surges through the arch, foam collars every rock it meets, and spray and mist burst skyward each time a wave breaks on the cliff foot. Layered strata, grassy cliff-top with wildflowers.

name: tide-pool
title: Tide Pools
blurb: Rocky intertidal shelf where swell washes over the seaward lip while the pools behind stay glassy, stirred only by drips and wind ripples. Starfish, anemones with swaying tentacles, sea urchins, mussel beds, barnacles, kelp ribbons and a scuttling crab.

name: coral-reef
title: Coral Reef
blurb: Sunlit reef patch: rippled sand, reef rock, brain, staghorn, table and lettuce corals, sea fans and tube sponges, a giant clam and an anemone with its clownfish. Schools of fish circle the reef, bubbles rise to a translucent swell, and caustic light nets dance over everything. A bleaching slider drains the colour from the corals.

name: kelp-forest
title: Kelp Forest
blurb: Giant kelp rising from a rocky reef to a floating canopy. Every stalk, blade and gas bulb leans and streams with the current; fish school through the columns, urchins graze the boulders, light nets ripple across the floor and a sea otter naps on its back at the surface.

name: iceberg
title: Iceberg & Floes
blurb: A drifting iceberg built to scale — the submerged keel is several times the visible freeboard (see it through the cut-away). Tabular, pinnacle, dome, wedge or dry-dock shapes with blue-ice veins and a wave-cut notch. Meltwater drips from the rim, a slab periodically calves into the sea with a splash and ripple ring, and pancake floes bob around it.

name: river-channel
title: River Channel
blurb: Meandering river reach carved into a floodplain. The cross-section is asymmetric — a deep, steep cut-bank on the outside of every bend and a shallow sandy point bar inside — and the current runs fastest mid-channel and around the outer bend. Boulders raise pillow waves and trail foam wakes, leaves and twigs drift downstream, reeds fringe the banks and riparian trees line the floodplain. Ports at both ends chain reaches together.

name: waterfall
title: Waterfall
blurb: A river runs across a plateau, accelerates over the lip and falls on a true ballistic arc (throw distance from the lip velocity, √(2h/g) fall time) into a churning plunge pool. Falling sheets carry downward-racing streaks, the pool boils with foam and continuous impact ripples, spray is flung outward and mist billows and drifts; the outflow leaves downstream. Plunge, horsetail or segmented styles.

name: rapids-cascade
title: Rapids & Cascade
blurb: A steep river reach stepping down rock ledges: glassy V-shaped tongues accelerate into each drop, hydraulic jumps boil white below it, trains of standing waves follow, and boulders push up pillows and trail foamy wakes while spray hangs over the steps. Total drop, number of steps, width and flow are all parametric.

name: mountain-brook
title: Mountain Brook
blurb: A small forest stream tumbling down a mossy slope: mini cascades over rock steps, riffles around stepping stones, a log footbridge, ferns and conifers, needles and leaves riding the current. Small scale — ankle-deep water, knee-high drops.

name: river-delta
title: River Delta
blurb: Where a river meets the sea and drops its load: the main stem splits into braided distributaries that fan across a low marshy plain, slowing as they spread; levees, sandbars and mud flats build between them, a brown sediment plume stains the sea off every mouth and small waves wash the delta front.

name: whirlpool
title: Whirlpool
blurb: A maelstrom: the sea surface sags into a vortex funnel (Rankine profile) while concentric bands of spiral foam spin faster the closer they are to the eye — free-vortex differential rotation — and flotsam spirals inward and is swallowed. Spin direction, depth, radius and arm count are parametric.

name: beaver-dam
title: Beaver Dam & Pond
blurb: Ecosystem engineering: a curved dam of woven sticks and mud backs a stream up into a still pond, drowning the old trees into grey snags. Water trickles over and seeps through the crest into the lower stream, a stick lodge rises from the pond and a beaver patrols with a V-shaped wake spreading behind it. Lily pads and cattails fringe the edges.

name: lake-pond
title: Lake & Pond
blurb: A still lake in a meadow basin: wind riffles scud across the surface, a shallow littoral shelf glows lighter than the deep middle, lily pads bob with their flowers, reeds and cattails lean in the breeze, a jetty stands on posts that ring the water, and now and then a fish leaps out and splashes back, printing ripple rings.

name: marsh-wetland
title: Marsh & Wetland
blurb: A freshwater marsh: a mosaic of shallow pools and winding channels between sedge hummocks and mudflats, duckweed rafts drifting on the water, reeds and cattails rippling in the wind, marsh-gas bubbles plopping up through the ooze, a heron fishing in the shallows and a raised boardwalk crossing it all.

name: mangrove-swamp
title: Mangrove Swamp
blurb: Tidal mangrove forest: trees stand on arching stilt roots over brackish water, pencil-like pneumatophores poke up from the mud to breathe, and the tide floods and drains the channels — set it high to drown the roots or low to expose the mud. A slow tidal current carries leaves between the trunks and small fish school in the shade.

name: frozen-lake
title: Frozen Lake
blurb: A lake locked under ice: a translucent sheet webbed with dark cracks and a jagged pressure ridge, wind-sculpted snow drifts, an augered fishing hole where open water still ripples, a little ice-fishing shelter, and an open lead where a stream keeps the ice from closing. Fine snow drifts down.

name: glacier-tongue
title: Glacier Tongue
blurb: A valley glacier creeping down a U-shaped trough: transverse crevasse fields where the ice stretches over steps, dark medial-moraine stripes, rubble lateral moraines, a supraglacial meltwater stream that disappears down a moulin, and a snout whose ice-cave portal releases the milky meltwater river into a proglacial lake dotted with bergy bits.

name: cave-pool
title: Cave & Drip Pool
blurb: A limestone cave chamber opened like a diorama: stalactites hang from the vault, stalagmites rise to meet them (some already fused into columns), flowstone curtains drape the walls and rimstone dams ring a crystal-clear pool. Drops fall from the dripping tips and each impact prints a ripple ring exactly when it lands. Glow-worms twinkle on the ceiling and calcite crystals sparkle at the water's edge.

name: groundwater-cutaway
title: Groundwater Cut-away
blurb: An educational block diagram of the hidden half of the water cycle: rain soaks through the unsaturated zone down to the water table, groundwater creeps through the saturated aquifer toward a gaining river, a confining clay layer seals a deeper confined aquifer above bedrock, a pumped well draws the water table into a cone of depression and a spring seeps out where the table meets the hillside. Animated recharge, flow and labelled layers.

name: geyser
title: Geyser Basin
blurb: A geothermal basin around a sinter cone: the vent pool simmers and surges, then the geyser erupts on a timed cycle — a column of water shoots to the set height and rains back, a steam cloud billows and drifts off — before falling quiet again. Rainbow-ringed hot pools (blue centres grading through green, yellow and orange microbial mats), steaming fumaroles and runoff channels complete the scene.

name: hot-spring-terraces
title: Hot Spring Terraces
blurb: Travertine terraces built by mineral-rich hot water: a steaming source pool spills down a staircase of scalloped rimmed basins, thin sheets cascading over every lip into the next pool. Colours grade from orange microbial mats at the hot source to milky turquoise pools on white travertine below.

name: rain-cloud
title: Rain Cloud & Precipitation
blurb: A cloud that actually precipitates: a lumpy cumulus/cumulonimbus mass, dark at the base and bright on top, releases rain, drizzle, snow, hail or sleet that falls at its real terminal speed (rain ≈ 7 m/s, snow ≈ 1 m/s), slants with the wind and bursts into splash rings on the ground below. Optional lightning forks flicker through the cloud.

name: fog-bank
title: Fog Bank & Mist
blurb: Low-lying fog: soft translucent billows hug the ground, drift downwind, swell and dissolve, and endlessly re-form upwind. Tune it from wisps of morning mist over a pond to a thick advection fog bank rolling in off the sea or valley fog pooled between hills.

name: waterspout
title: Waterspout
blurb: A tornado over water: a rotating, gently snaking condensation funnel descends from a dark cloud base, and where it touches the sea a spinning spray vortex flings droplets outward and up while a dark spot of spiralling foam marks the water surface around its foot.

name: rainbow
title: Rainbow
blurb: Sunlight refracted through raindrops: a primary bow (red outside, violet inside, ≈42°) and an optional fainter secondary bow with reversed colours (≈51°). The arc tapers at its feet, can billboard toward the camera, fades away at night or turns into a pale moonbow.

name: puddles
title: Rain Puddles
blurb: A rain-soaked patch of street: cobbles, flagstones, asphalt or packed dirt darkened by wetness, puddles pooled in every hollow and pocked by raindrop rings and splash crowns, a gutter carrying runoff into a swirling drain grate, and an optional street lamp glowing at night.

name: water-mill
title: Water Mill
blurb: A working grist mill. Water runs along a timber flume on trestles and pours onto an overshot wheel (or a stream drives the paddles of an undershot wheel); the wheel's speed follows the flow (ω = v / r), filled buckets spill as they descend and the tailrace churns away. The stone-and-timber mill house is hollow and enterable: real door and window openings, plank floors, an upper storey, millstones and pit wheel turning on the same axle inside, and glowing windows at night.

name: dam-spillway
title: Dam & Spillway
blurb: A concrete gravity dam (optionally arched in plan) impounds a reservoir across a valley. Raise the radial gates and water pours over the ogee crest, races down the spillway chute and slams into a stilling basin where a hydraulic jump boils white before the river carries on. A crest road with lamps, gate piers and a hollow powerhouse at the toe with turbine outflows complete it.

name: canal-lock
title: Canal Lock
blurb: A working pound lock that lifts boats between two canal levels. On its automatic cycle the lower mitre gates swing open, close, the upper paddles jet water in and the chamber fills; the upper gates open, close, and the lower paddles drain it back down with turbulence boiling into the lower pound. The chamber surface is exposed so a boat placed inside rises and falls with it. Balance beams, bollards, ladders and a hollow lock-keeper's hut.

name: stone-aqueduct
title: Stone Aqueduct
blurb: A Roman-style arcade carrying water across a valley on one to three tiers of real arched openings, the upper tiers stepping to twice as many arches. The open channel (specus) on top carries a steady flow; set it ruined and the far end crumbles, fallen blocks litter the ground and the water spills from the broken channel in a falling sheet. A stream winds beneath the central arch.

name: stone-bridge
title: Stone Arch Bridge
blurb: A masonry road bridge striding across a river on segmental arches. The whole elevation is one extruded outline with true arch openings, faced with voussoir rings; pointed cutwaters split the current on the upstream side, where pillows of water pile up, while foamy V-wakes trail downstream of every pier. Parapets, a cobbled deck, approach banks and optional lamps.

name: water-well
title: Village Well
blurb: A stone well with a shingled roof and windlass. On its cycle the crank turns, the rope pays out and the bucket drops down the shaft, splashes into the water far below (a ripple ring spreads across the dark surface), then winds back up dripping all the way.

name: hand-pump-trough
title: Hand Pump & Trough
blurb: A cast-iron pitcher pump on a stone plinth: the lever rocks, the plunger rod rides up and down and every stroke gushes a stream from the spout into a trough, whose surface ripples where it lands; the brimming trough overflows through a notch into a puddle.

name: fountain-plaza
title: Fountain Plaza
blurb: A tiered civic fountain: a central jet climbs and showers back into the top bowl, every bowl brims and overflows in scalloped curtains to the tier below, and a ring of rim nozzles throws true ballistic arcs that land in the pool — each landing point ripples. Checker paving, benches facing the water, lamp posts, coins glinting on the basin floor and underwater lights for the evening.

name: water-tower
title: Water Tower
blurb: An elevated storage tank that keeps a town's taps pressurised: braced steel legs, a central riser pipe, a catwalk with railing and access ladder, a cylindrical, spherical or wooden-barrel tank with the town name wrapped around it, a blinking aviation light — and an overflow pipe that periodically gushes into a splash basin at the foot.

name: rice-terraces
title: Rice Terraces
blurb: Curving terraced paddies stepping down a hillside, each a flooded mirror held in by a mud bund. A bamboo flume pours irrigation water into the top terrace; from there it trickles through notches cut in each bund and runs down the riser to the paddy below, ringing the water where it lands. Rice grows in tufted rows that ripple in the breeze — from bare mirrors to tall golden harvest.

name: lighthouse
title: Lighthouse
blurb: A striped lighthouse on a wave-washed islet. The tower is truly hollow — the door and window slots are real openings through the wall, and a spiral stair winds up the inside around a newel — topped by a gallery, a glazed lantern room and a cupola. At night the lamp blazes and twin beams sweep the sea; by day swell rolls in, foam collars the rocks and spray bursts against them.

name: wooden-pier
title: Wooden Pier
blurb: A timber pier marching out from the beach on paired piles: X-braced bents, stringers and plank decking, railings, bollards, a life ring, a ladder down to the water, lamp posts and an optional T-head. Swell rolls in beneath it, foam collars swirl around every pile, ripple rings spread from the piles in deeper water, and the cut-away sea walls ride the waves.

name: lifeguard-tower
title: Lifeguard Tower
blurb: A raised beach lifeguard station: braced stilts lift an enterable hut (real door opening, glazed side and front windows, an open lookout facing the sea, plank floor and ceiling), a railed deck wraps around it, a ramp runs down to the sand, red and yellow flags snap in the sea breeze, and a rescue buoy, rescue tube and surfboard stand ready. The tower name is lettered over the door.

name: rowboat
title: Rowboat
blurb: A clinker-built wooden rowing boat: a lofted lapstrake hull with steamed ribs, keelson, thwarts, floorboards, bronze oarlocks and a painter trailing in the water. A rower pulls a real stroke cycle — blades bite at the catch (ripple rings), drive aft, lift at the finish (swirling puddles) and recover — while the hull bobs, pitches and rolls on the swell and a faint wake trails astern. Floats on its own preview patch or on any water asset.

name: sailboat
title: Sailboat
blurb: A cruising sloop under sail: lofted hull with fin keel and bulb, spade rudder and tiller, a sunken cockpit with benches and winches, a cabin trunk with portlights and a sliding hatch, mast, spreaders and standing rigging, stanchions and lifelines. The cambered mainsail and genoa set on either tack for any point of sail — the boom swings across, the sails' belly flips to leeward, the boat heels to the breeze and the leech flutters — while bow waves and a Kelvin wake stream astern. Furl the sails to lie at anchor.

name: kayak
title: Sea Kayak
blurb: A touring sea kayak: a slim lofted hull with strong rocker, crowned deck, a smooth oval cockpit with a raised coaming and spray deck, fore and aft hatches, perimeter lines and bungees, carry toggles and a skeg. A paddler drives a feathered double-bladed paddle in a continuous left-right rhythm — each blade dips mid-stroke, rings spread where it enters — while the torso rotates with the stroke, the hull rolls gently and bow waves and a slim wake follow.

name: fishing-boat
title: Fishing Boat
blurb: A working inshore trawler: flared lofted hull with bulwarks, boot-top and rubbing strake, and an enterable wheelhouse — real door and window openings, console, wheel, chair and chart table inside, an interior lamp for night. Outrigger booms hinge down to fish with their stays and tow wires, a net drum turns on the stern gantry (or a longliner's buoy flags / a crabber's pot stack), the propeller spins and the exhaust puffs smoke. Navigation and deck lights, fenders, life rings, a windlass and anchor, and the boat's name on bows and transom. Bow waves and prop wash trail astern.

name: channel-buoy
title: Navigation Buoy
blurb: Channel markers that ride the swell on a hanging chain: can, nun, lighted lattice-tower, spar and mooring buoys with numbers wrapped on, counterweights below the waterline and a concrete sinker on the seabed. Lighted buoys flash a real characteristic — flash, quick, isophase, occulting or long-flash at any period — carry a radar reflector and an optional bell whose clappers swing as the buoy rolls. Colourways for green/red lateral, cardinal, safe-water and special marks.

name: floating-dock
title: Floating Dock
blurb: A modular marina pontoon: timber-decked sections on float drums, each riding the swell independently and guided by hoops sliding on fixed piles, joined by hinge plates, with cleats, rubber bumper strips and a lamp post. A gangway hinged at a concrete shore abutment tilts to follow the first section as it rises and falls. Lay it out straight, as an L, or as a T-head.

name: fish-school
title: Fish School
blurb: A school of fish as one instanced draw call — sardines, tuna, clownfish, koi, trout or neon tetras, each with its own body proportions and markings — swimming in formation on a loop, a figure-eight, or milling in a tight bait ball, every fish wagging as it turns. Shown inside a cut-away aquarium of sand, rocks and swaying weed with caustics rippling over the floor and a bubbler; switch the tank off to drop the school into any lake, reef or ocean.

name: water-lilies
title: Water Lilies
blurb: A drifting colony of water lilies: notched, gently cupped pads (or giant rimmed Victoria-style pads), layered open blooms and closed buds, each tethered by a stem to the muddy bottom and riding whatever water it floats on. A frog sits on a pad and leaps from pad to pad — ripples ring out at take-off and landing — while dragonflies dart, hover and dip their tails to the surface.

name: reed-bed
title: Reed Bed
blurb: A lakeshore reed bed in a cut-away diorama: a muddy bank shelving into shallow water, dense stands of feathery-plumed common reed, cattails with brown seed heads, dark rushes and yellow flag irises, all bending in the wind. Reeds thin out into deeper water, ripple rings spread from stems and from rising fish, and a red-winged blackbird clings to a swaying cattail.

name: duck-family
title: Duck Family
blurb: A mother duck leads her ducklings in a bobbing line around the pond with the drake paddling alongside; every bird trails its own little V-wake and ring of ripples, and now and then the mother tips up to dabble, tail in the air. Switch species to a swan pair with grey cygnets. Floats on its own pond patch or rides any water asset.

name: whale
title: Whale
blurb: A humpback, orca or blue whale on a long loop through open water, built from articulated body, tail-stock and fluke segments that beat as it swims, with pectoral flippers, dorsal fin, ventral grooves and markings per species. Its cycle: cruise at depth, rise until the back breaks the surface, blow twice (misty spouts), arch and raise its flukes — water streaming off them — and sound. In breach mode every other cycle it launches clear of the sea, twists and crashes back in a ring of spray.

name: seagull-flock
title: Seagulls
blurb: A flock of gulls over the water: fliers wheel on banked soaring circles at different heights, gliding with bursts of flapping on gull-bent wings; one plunges for a fish now and then — a splash and a ring of ripples — and climbs away. Others float on the swell with folded wings, and a few stand sentry on mooring posts. Instanced bodies and wings keep the whole flock to a handful of draw calls.

name: terrain-tile
title: Terrain Tile
blurb: A configurable ground tile for composing water scenes: meadow, rolling hills, dunes, terraced rocky upland, snowfield or patchwork farmland with hedgerows. Any hollow below the water level fills as a lake with a foamy, sandy shoreline and cut-away water walls; a dirt path winds across; grass tufts that sway in the wind, wildflowers and stones are scattered to suit. Edge blending flattens the border to y = 0 so tiles butt seamlessly against each other and against the water assets.

name: tree-grove
title: Tree Grove
blurb: A stand of trees for lakeshores, riverbanks and islands — pines, broadleaves, white birches, weeping willows trailing curtains of strands, or coconut palms, mixed or pure — with canopies that sway in the wind, an understorey of bushes, ferns and grass, mossy fallen logs and a ground patch. Seasonal colourways from spring blossom to autumn gold and winter snow.

name: boulder-cluster
title: Boulder Cluster
blurb: Rocks for shorelines, rivers and coasts: rounded glacial boulders, hexagonal basalt columns or layered sedimentary slabs, with moss and lichen on their tops and pebbles around them. Set them in water and they darken below the waterline, the current wraps foam collars round each rock and drags foamy wakes and ripples downstream (+X), with cut-away water walls showing the bed.

name: swimming-pool
title: Swimming Pool
blurb: An inground pool in a cut-away diorama: rectangular, lap (with floor lane lines and floating lane ropes), round or kidney-shaped, sloping from the shallow end to the diving well, lined with tiles and a waterline mosaic band, edged with coping and set in a paver deck. Clear water throws caustics across the floor; entry steps, a grab-rail ladder and a springboard that flexes; a raised spa spills a sheet of water into the pool; an inflatable ring drifts on the ripples; underwater lights, sun loungers and an umbrella for the evening.
